speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the skin lesions in detail and tell me when the fever and wrist pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall being bitten by a tick while camping, or have you noticed a circular, expanding rash at the site of a potential bite? I also need to know if the wrist swelling is warm to the touch and if you have any joint stiffness in the morning.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent travel to Minnesota and the specific violaceous vesiculopustular lesions, I suspect a tick-borne illness like Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever or Ehrlichiosis. REQUEST TEST: Tick-borne panel, CBC, and CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a known history of sickle cell trait or disease, and have you recently experienced any respiratory infections or upper respiratory symptoms? I am concerned about acute chest syndrome or osteomyelitis given the fever, elevated white blood cell count, and characteristic skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any lesions on your palms or soles, and do you have a headache or nausea? I also need to confirm if you have had any recent unprotected sexual intercourse, as these symptoms strongly suggest secondary syphilis. REQUEST TEST: Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR) and VDRL.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR): Not available in current data. VDRL: Not available in current data.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands, combined with the acute monoarthritis and fever, I am concerned about a sexually transmitted infection like Chancroid or Granuloma Inguinale, though the joint involvement is atypical. I need to rule out septic arthritis caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which can present with dermatitis and tenosynovitis. REQUEST TEST: Joint aspirate for Gram stain and culture, and Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint aspiration: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen. STI Screen: Gonorrhea: Positive, Chlamydia: Negative, HIV: Negative. Blood Cultures: Pending at the time of examination.

speaker: Doctor
text: The joint aspiration confirming Gram-negative diplococci and the positive NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae definitively diagnose Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
